title: Partial-token detection & state resync for streaming failover
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Summary: During the capacity event on 2026-02-18 we observed a class of streaming failures where clients received truncated token sequences and subsequently reconnected, causing duplicate or missing output and inconsistent KV cache state on the server. This ticket captures the follow-up action items to reliably detect partial-token delivery, reconcile client/server state, and implement a graceful failover path that preserves application-level correctness.
background: Root cause analysis from incident: (1) aggressive backpressure combined with connection churn resulted in stream writes being cut mid-token; (2) reconnect logic retried from last-seen byte instead of last-seen token boundary; (3) server-side KV cache eviction and request routing to different serving nodes produced token-generation divergence on retry. Mitigations during the incident reduced customer-visible failures but left edge cases where partial tokens were exposed to SDKs and downstream apps.
acceptance_criteria: Server emits explicit token-boundary markers in stream frames (protocol update) or ensures atomic token frame emission
Reconnect logic retries at token boundary or requests a replay from server when ambiguity detected
KV cache reconciliation runbook exists: a safe resync RPC that both invalidates and replenishes cache without user-visible duplication
Automated integration test that simulates mid-token drop and asserts deterministic output after reconnects
tasks: Design: define token-boundary wire format and backward-compatible framing (owner: Liam Chen, due 2026-03-05)
Runtime: implement atomic token framing and server-side check to never expose partial tokens (owner: Priya Nair, due 2026-03-12)
SDKs: add client-side reconnect heuristics to detect partial-token receipts and request a replay (owners: Rahul Desai / Maya Ortiz, due 2026-03-16)
KV cache: implement resync endpoint + reconciliation procedure and add metrics for cache divergence events (owner: Jonas Berg, due 2026-03-18)
Observability: dashboard for partial-token rate, reconnects per-tenant, and replay success rate (owner: SRE Oncall, due 2026-03-13)
E2E tests: chaos test that simulates mid-stream disconnects across all serving topologies (owner: qa-infra, due 2026-03-19)
Rollout: feature-flag the framing change and stage in hosted -> dedicated -> private (owner: Release Eng, due 2026-04-01)
Docs: SDK migration guide & runbook for customers to handle replay semantics (owner: Developer Experience, due 2026-03-22)
updates: 2026-02-26: Incident postmortem published to Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.example/incidents/2026-02-18-streaming-capacity (initial RCA and mitigation list).

2026-03-02: Design review completed; chosen approach is explicit token-framing rather than attempting to infer boundaries from UTF-8 sequences to avoid language/model edge cases. Trade-off: small wire-protocol change vs higher protocol clarity.

2026-03-04: Prototype server framing implemented in branch feat/atomic-token-frames. Initial microbench shows <1% throughput regression at 2048 context length on A100; profiling indicates serialization CPU cost is dominant and can be optimized.
2026-03-06: SDK team added heuristic: if last received frame does not end with token-complete marker, request a deterministic replay RPC. Added feature flag for immediate opt-in.

2026-03-09: KV cache resync RPC v1 design posted in internal docs and reviewed by Core Runtime and SRE. Concerns raised about coordination during multi-region failover; follow-up to add optimistic locking.

2026-03-11: First integration tests for mid-token disconnects pass in single-node mode; failing in multi-node routing scenarios due to stale routing table TTLs. Added ENG-33902 to address stale routing TTLs.
2026-03-13: Security review not required for protocol framing, but compliance requested that replay RPC be auditable. Added audit-log requirement to KV cache task.
Note: updated_at advanced to reflect current progress and test results.
risks_and_tradeoffs: Options considered: (A) strict token framing (chosen) — small wire change, deterministic semantics; (B) best-effort UTF-8/byte heuristics — no protocol change but brittle across tokenizers/encodings; (C) server-side buffering until stable token end — adds latency. We selected A to minimize client complexity and to enable deterministic replays even across model/hardware differences. Risk: incremental CPU overhead; mitigations: optimize serialization and gate behind FF until performance validated.
postmortem_action_items: Short-term: roll out SDK FF to opt-in customers and triage edge cases (owner: SDK, due 2026-03-16)
Medium-term: full runtime rollout with optimized serialization and canary across 5% host traffic (owner: Runtime, due 2026-03-30)
Long-term: add automatic capacity-aware throttles that detect mid-token backpressure and shift requests to queued replay mode before dropping connections (owner: Serving Team, due 2026-05-01)
qa_notes: E2E tests must cover: (1) mid-token TCP disconnect; (2) reconnect to same node vs different node; (3) KV cache resync under eviction pressure; (4) replay idempotency under duplicate frames. Use synthetic model that echoes tokens with sequence IDs for deterministic assertions.
next_steps: Complete multi-node routing TTL fix (ENG-33902), finish server perf optimizations, and schedule canary deploy. Coordinate with Support for customer communications and create customer-facing FAQ explaining replay semantics.
notes_for_support: If customers report duplicated tokens after reconnect, ask for: full stream logs, SDK version, whether FF for replay was enabled, and timestamp of disconnect. Recommend enabling FF to gather telemetry before full rollout.
estimated_impact_reduction: Expected to reduce customer-visible partial-token incidents by >=95% after full rollout; metric: partial-token-rate per 100k streams.
visibility: Public to internal engineering, postmortem shared with CS and SRE teams. Customer-facing summary slated after canary completes.
